sections.history: Horanadu is a small village in the Western Ghats of Chikkamagaluru district, set among coffee estates and rainforest on the bank of the Bhadra river, not far from Kudremukh. Its temple to Annapoorneshwari is one of the most loved goddess shrines of the Malnad. Tradition carries its sanctity back to the sage Agastya, and Adi Shankaracharya is remembered as having renewed its spiritual power. For about four hundred years a hereditary family of dharmakartas has conducted its worship. In 1973 the temple was renovated under the trustee D. B. Venkatasubba Jois, and a new image of the Goddess was consecrated on the festival of Akshaya Tritiya.
sections.architecture: The temple stands in a forest clearing above the river, its buildings framed by the green slopes of the Ghats. At its heart is the sanctum of Annapoorneshwari, whose image is of gold and draws the eye of every devotee who reaches the threshold. Around it are the halls and kitchens of a working pilgrim centre, for at Horanadu the dining hall matters almost as much as the shrine: here the Goddess's gift of food is served, day after day, to all who come.
sections.legends: Annapoorna is the form of Parvati who holds the ladle and vessel of plenty, the mother who ensures that no one in the world goes hungry; a well-loved story tells how even Shiva came to her as a mendicant to receive alms of food. Horanadu's tradition says that the sage Agastya first consecrated the Goddess here, and that Adi Shankaracharya later renewed the shrine. Devotees believe that one who prays to her here will never lack food.
sections.festivals: Akshaya Tritiya, held to be the Goddess's birthday and the anniversary of the 1973 consecration, is the chief festival. The Rathotsava, the chariot festival of about five days, falls in February or March, and Navaratri is celebrated with special worship in the autumn. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Horanadu is known above all for annadana: every visitor is fed by the temple, with meals served several times a day, so pilgrims leave having received the Goddess's prasada as a meal. The winding drive through the misty hills is part of the journey, and many combine the visit with Kalasa, Sringeri and the temples of the coast.

visit.timings: Open daily from early morning to night, with a break in the afternoon; weekends, Akshaya Tritiya and the festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Traditional dress is expected and the temple's dress rules are strictly observed; follow the posted guidance at the entrance. Footwear is removed before entering.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted in the sanctum; follow the posted rules elsewhere in the temple.
visit.gettingThere: Horanadu is about 10 km from Kalasa and roughly 95 km from Chikkamagaluru by hill roads through the Ghats; Chikkamagaluru has the nearest railway station, and Mangaluru International Airport is the nearest major airport. Buses run from Kalasa, Chikkamagaluru and Mangaluru.
